analysis.title: weekly mash :: 2027 Outlooks (Mark Wilson, 13 Nov 2026)
key_insights: GS expects stable global growth of 2.8% in 2027 versus 2.7% in 2026, with slowing inflation. Uncertainty and downside risks are driven mainly by Middle East/energy and a slowing AI investment boom.
GS expects 2 more Fed hikes and 1 from the ECB in 2027, below what markets now price. GS thinks both central banks will be cutting by the end of the year.
GS is overweight US and Japanese equities, neutral Asia/EM, and underweight Europe. It also downgrades European banks after a strong run.

Earnings growth slows in 2027: US EPS growth falls from 36% to 11%, Europe from 18% to 7%, Japan from 24% to 9%. GS says higher real rates, wider credit spreads and peaking AI investment matter more for profits and equities than GDP.
GS is above consensus on US GDP growth at 2.4% versus 2.2%, supported by resilient investment. US equities have de-rated while profitability remains superior.

Global AI investment rises from $1.1tn in 2026 to $1.8tn in 2027, adding 0.4pp to global GDP growth, but the incremental investment impulse peaks in 1H27. GS says equity markets have already priced much of this in after data-center buildout concerns and the Democratic midterm sweep.

GS sees the 10y UST yield at 4.6% by end 2027. It says central bank pricing is too hawkish versus its baseline, bond valuations are cheap and positioning is underweight. Bonds should regain hedging value as supply shocks give way to demand risks.

GS calls Europe a good AI hedge. European indices were resilient through recent AI sell-offs, US investors are adding European exposure, and a 5.5% FCF yield, buybacks and shrinking net equity supply provide support. GS still expects lower 2027 index returns in Europe than in the US or Asia.

GS expects Brent to fall towards $78/bbl by end 2027. A 10% rise in oil has historically taken about 1% off European valuations. Lower oil and yields favor Retailers, Utilities, Telecoms, UK Real Estate and the DAX, and hurt Energy, Banks and Insurance.

Global Tech trades around the 20th percentile of its 20-year valuation range. Hyperscalers trade on 19.7x forward P/E with their premium to the S&P 500 almost eliminated. European Tech offers about 28% 2027 EPS growth at under 1x PEG. Traditional Value is near the 90th percentile of its valuation range.

GS favors Growth with valuation discipline and selective Defensives rather than a broad defensive rotation. Preferred areas are US Hyperscalers, Healthcare, Power and Buyback Aristocrats, plus European Tech, Telecoms and Utilities and selective Asian AI exposure.

Wilson notes the prior week's market action: Thursday saw the largest ever notional one-day stock market decline, equities recovered by Wednesday, then fell again on worsening inflation news, higher yields and the ejection of the founder/CEO of the world's largest company.

Wilson notes France's CAC-40 was outperforming GS's basket of AI winners over the last 12 months as of last week, and European banks have outperformed the Mag7 over 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 years. He expects Europe to be highly topical, with political shifts (Spain in two weeks) and falling energy prices on one side and rising government bond yields on the other.

risk_factors: Slowing AI investment boom, with the investment impulse peaking in 1H27.
Higher real rates and wider credit spreads weighing on profits.
Surging government bond yields creating vulnerabilities for numerous European countries.
Worsening inflation news and higher yields, per Wilson's account of last week.
vol_and_positioning: Thursday of the prior week saw the largest ever notional one-day stock market decline, per Wilson.
Bond positioning is described as underweight, supporting the duration call.
US investors are already increasing European exposure.
geopolitical: Middle East/energy uncertainty is a main source of downside risk in the GS 2027 outlooks.
Further de-escalation would lower energy prices and yields, disproportionately helping Europe.
Europe is likely to see a meaningful political shift, starting with Spain in two weeks, in the opposite direction from the US midterms' move from Right to Left.
US midterms moved the US politically from Right to Left (Democratic sweep).

tension_points.bull_case: Europe is the clearest economic beneficiary of falling energy prices (Brent towards $78), is seen as a good AI hedge, has a 5.5% FCF yield and buybacks, and US investors are already rotating in.
tension_points.bear_case: GS expects lower 2027 index returns in Europe than the US or Asia. EPS growth slows from 18% to 7%, and surging government bond yields create vulnerabilities for numerous European countries.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Further de-escalation failing to deliver lower energy prices and yields, which GS says would be the disproportionate help for Europe.
